presentingComplaint: Progressive dry cough and exertional breathlessness for 3 months with fatigue
history: 34-year-old woman, non-smoker, with 3 months of dry cough, gradually worsening exertional dyspnea, generalised fatigue and low-grade intermittent fever. Reports tender red nodules over both shins that appeared 6 weeks ago (subsequently faded), and 4 kg unintentional weight loss. No haemoptysis, no purulent sputum, no night sweats of drenching type, no TB contact. No occupational dust/beryllium exposure. Mild bilateral ankle discomfort. No prior lung disease. Not immunocompromised, no recent travel to malaria/TB-endemic setting beyond usual residence.
examination: Comfortable at rest, mildly tachypneic on exertion. Faint residual erythema nodosum over anterior shins. Bilateral non-tender palpable cervical lymphadenopathy. Chest auscultation largely clear (few fine end-inspiratory crackles at bases). No clubbing. No hepatosplenomegaly. No skin plaques on face, no lupus pernio. Eyes: no anterior uveitis on bedside exam. Cardiovascular exam normal, no murmur; JVP not raised.
imaging: CXR: bilateral symmetric hilar lymphadenopathy with fine reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates (Scadding stage II). HRCT thorax: bilateral hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy with perilymphatic micronodules along bronchovascular bundles and upper-zone predominance.
microbiology: Sputum AFB smear negative x2; sputum culture pending/negative. n/a for bacterial pathogen.
finalDiagnosis: Sarcoidosis (Scadding stage II, with Löfgren-type features)
citations: ATS/ERS/WASOG Statement on Sarcoidosis (ATS Diagnosis and Detection of Sarcoidosis 2020)
contraindications: Avoid empiric anti-TB therapy until TB excluded (AFB/culture/biopsy) as steroids can worsen active TB
Hypercalcemia: avoid vitamin D / calcium supplementation and excess sun exposure
If corticosteroids started, monitor glucose and bone health
edgeCases: Löfgren syndrome (bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy + erythema nodosum + arthralgia/fever) can be diagnosed clinically without biopsy and carries excellent prognosis
Cardiac or neurosarcoidosis may present without prominent pulmonary symptoms and requires directed workup
Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy mandates exclusion of TB and lymphoma before attributing to sarcoid, especially in TB-endemic regions
expectedMaiK: Classic sarcoidosis: bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, dry cough/dyspnea, erythema nodosum, elevated ACE and hypercalcemia in a young adult. Prioritise excluding TB and lymphoma; confirm with non-necrotising granulomas on nodal/lung biopsy and reserve corticosteroids for symptomatic or organ-threatening disease.
expectedNextQuestions: Any eye symptoms (red eye, blurring) suggesting uveitis, or palpitations/syncope suggesting cardiac involvement?
Any occupational beryllium/organic dust exposure or TB contact?
expectedInvestigations: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided lymph node biopsy (EBUS-TBNA) for non-caseating granulomas
Serum ACE and 24h urinary calcium, ophthalmology slit-lamp exam, ECG (screen cardiac sarcoid)
Exclude TB: sputum AFB/culture and IGRA; biopsy stain/culture for AFB

investigations: Sputum AFB / IGRA to exclude TB
